The paper leaves out Supplementary Information and the appendix, so Table A1.2 isn't available to check directly. The main text does describe validation against an independent set of 4.87M random points balanced on the dependent variable, covering regeneration from 2000 to 2016. The 2030 predictions use newer covariates, 2018 tree cover and 2015 land cover, so I'm looking at whether the validation was run against the model fit with the 2000 covariates.

I'm checking whether the validation used the model fit with 2000-era covariates, since the 2030 predictions swapped in newer ones. The paper's main text describes the validation on an independent random sample, but it's not clear which covariate version that model used. Even so, the broader point holds: nothing here is a temporal out-of-sample test, and accuracy drops with distance from the training points.

I'm weighing whether the calibration of the probabilities matters more than the accuracy figure, since those probabilities were summed to reach the 215 Mha total. The verdict looks like "partly right": the main text supports the general point that validation isn't a test of forward prediction, but the specific claim about the table can't be confirmed from this document. I'd rate it important, since the 2030 headline and the 87.9% accuracy are used to justify the result.
